claims.text: Group IV-containing refractory high-entropy alloys are susceptible to oxygen uptake during processing.
Oxygen uptake in the target alloys causes brittle alpha-HCP phase precipitation.
The hydride precursor powder can have an initial oxygen content below 0.1 mass percent.
Hydride decomposition under vacuum followed by immediate hot extrusion can replace mechanical alloying or gas atomization.
A ramp below 5 °C/min to 600 °C followed by a 700 °C hold for two hours ensures complete hydrogen desorption without oxygen ingress.
Hot extrusion at 1100–1200 °C and a strain rate of 0.1 s^-1 will consolidate the material without catastrophic cracking.
Ultra-high-vacuum hydride decomposition will suppress TiO formation by preventing oxygen uptake.
Ultra-high-vacuum hydride decomposition will suppress brittle alpha-HCP phase formation.
Stepwise thermomechanical processing of the target NbMoTaWVTi alloy will form metastable coherent B2 or L21 nanoprecipitates.
Mechanical alloying can introduce approximately 1.07 wt% oxygen into a Group IV-containing refractory alloy powder.
Mechanically alloyed and SPS-processed NbMoTaWVTi can contain about 0.86 mass percent oxygen and fine TiO precipitates.
Fine TiO precipitates impede dislocation motion in a BCC NbMoTaWVTi matrix and increase strength.
TiO precipitates significantly decrease ductility and cause severe embrittlement in conventionally processed NbMoTaWVTi.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, thereby limiting premature cracking while retaining strengthening.
Non-coherent silicide or Laves precipitates can promote brittle fracture.
The proposed processing will produce a dense BCC bulk matrix containing coherent nanoprecipitates.
The processed alloy will have a yield strength above 600 MPa at 700 °C.
The processed alloy will have room-temperature ductility above 10 percent.
Residual hydrogen from incomplete hydride decomposition could form voids.
Insufficient cooling-rate control could promote brittle Laves phase formation.

contradictions.description: The outcome is described as a single-phase BCC material while also being described as containing coherent nanoprecipitates; a matrix plus a distinct precipitate phase is not strictly single-phase.

The experiment assigns Batch A to hydride decomposition and hot extrusion and Batch B to mechanical alloying and SPS, but then states that both receive identical thermal histories. The specified processing routes inherently involve different consolidation thermal histories unless 'identical' refers only to a later post-treatment.
